directAnswer: To check an SDK, verify its installation and version using the command line or the IDE's built-in tools, depending on your development environment.
summary: This guide provides steps to check the installation and version of an SDK across different platforms.

sections.heading: Checking SDK Installation
sections.body: Ensure that the SDK is properly installed on your system by using command line tools or IDE features.

sections.heading: Checking SDK Version
sections.body: Use specific commands or IDE options to retrieve the version of the SDK you have installed.

steps.title: Using Command Line
steps.detail: Open your terminal or command prompt and enter the command specific to your SDK, such as 'sdkmanager --list' for Android SDK or 'dotnet --version' for .NET SDK.

steps.title: Using IDE
steps.detail: In your IDE, navigate to the settings or preferences section, find the SDK settings, and check the version displayed there. Note that paths may vary by IDE version.

faqs.question: What should I do if the SDK is not installed?
faqs.answer: Follow the official installation guide for the SDK to download and install it correctly.

faqs.question: How can I update my SDK?
faqs.answer: Use the package manager or IDE options to update the SDK to the latest version available.

faqs.question: Are there any compatibility issues I should be aware of?
faqs.answer: Check the SDK documentation for compatibility notes regarding your development environment and other libraries.

caveats: SDK commands may vary based on the version and platform, so refer to the official documentation for the most accurate instructions.
